sentences.text:
Of 2023 Dated 13.3.2023 Under Sections ... vs Allowed on 17
August, 2023
17.08.2023
 tkm/ct 28 C.R.M. (A) 3494 of 2023
spl no. 22

In Re : An application for anticipatory bail under section 438 of the Code  of Criminal Procedure in connection with Krishanganj P.S case no. 89  of 2023 dated 13.3.2023 under sections 498A/325/306/506/34 IPC  And Allowed  In Re : Kalpana Karmakar & Anr. ...... petitioners  Mr. K K Mukherjee  Ms. Eshita Aich  ...... for the petitioners  Ms. Faria Hossain  Ms. Baisali Basu  Ms. Mamata Jana  ...... for the State  1.
Heard learned lawyer for the parties.
2. We have considered the materials on record.
Petitioners are the parents-in-law of one Pratima Karmakar.
There was a matrimonial dispute between Pratima and her husband Ananda.
As a result Pratima took refuge at her parental residence.
Ananda went there to bring back Pratima.
At that time he misbehaved with Pratima's brother who subsequently committed suicide.

Keeping in mind the extent of complicity of the petitioners in the crime, we are of the opinion custodial interrogation of the petitioners for progress of investigation is not necessary and they may be granted anticipatory bail.

3. Accordingly, we direct that in the event of arrest, the petitioners shall be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs. 10,000/- each with two sureties of like amount each, to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer and also be subject to the conditions as laid down under section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
4. Petitioners shall appear before the court below and pray for regular bail within four weeks from date.
5. The application being CRM (A) 3494 of 2023 is disposed of.

(Gaurang Kanth, J.) (Joymalya Bagchi, J.)
